thread:
incident-bot: ALERT: sudden spike in 5xx and token cost for /v1/generate on prod-us-west-2. Auto-escalation to #incidents (sev2). KPIs: 5xx rate 3.4% (baseline 0.1%), p95 latency 4.2s -> 9.8s, token throughput up 2.7x. Suspect: KV prefix cache growth and continuous-batching backlog. Paging oncall alice_oncall.

alice_oncall: I'm on it. pulling logs from serving runtime now. any recent rollouts? @devon_platform

devon_platform: we rolled a change to continuous_batching defaults to opt-in two hours ago (rollout 10%). No other infra deploys in last 30m. I see increased mem usage on kv-store nodes starting ~2599999600.

ben_sre: seeing a lot of small keys with similar prompthash prefixes. Heap surge on kvcache-03. Looks like cache TTLs didn't apply because tokenized keys changed shape — regen flood.

carmen_ml: Could be tokenizer rollout mismatch. We shipped an updated tokenizer normalization in model-serving config earlier this week. If tokenization changed, prompt-hash keys will be inconsistent and create lots of uniques -> cache blowup.

frank_engineer: confirming: logs show prompt_key length variance and a spike in unique prefix hashes. snippet:

```
2026-03-15T10:12:34Z SERVE prompt_key="usr:conv:tokenized:â\u001b" hash=0x9f4a... size=1234
2026-03-15T10:12:35Z KVPUT key=prompt:prefix:0x9f4a... ttl=0
```

frank_engineer: also seeing continuous-batching queue depth climb from 12 -> 1200 which amplifies downstream pressure.

alice_oncall: immediate mitigations we can do now?

ben_sre: plan: 1) pause continuous_batching on prod-facing pools, 2) reduce max_batch_size and window, 3) evict suspect prefix cache entries (short TTL), 4) enable fallback routing to dedicated predictable pools.

devon_platform: I can flip the flag via /ops/feature toggles. Proposed change:

```
continuous_batching: false
max_batch_size: 64  # from 256
batch_window_ms: 20  # from 100
prefix_cache_ttl: 300  # force eviction
```

alice_oncall: do it. roll out to prod-us-west-2 only first, watch.

devon_platform: running:

```
opsctl feature set continuous_batching=false --env prod-us-west-2
opsctl config set serving.max_batch_size=64 --env prod-us-west-2
opsctl config set serving.batch_window_ms=20 --env prod-us-west-2
opsctl config set kv.prefix_cache_tll=300 --env prod-us-west-2
```

incident-bot: Deploy started by devon_platform. Notifying oncall.

carmen_ml: also recommend invalidating prompthash mapping cache and trigger a controlled key scrub for keys older than 1h with pattern `prompt:prefix:*0x9f4a*` — but that's risky. Prefer TTL-based fast path.

frank_engineer: agreed. I'll push a hotfix to serving that disables local prefix caching and forces K/V canonicalization for 10 minutes.

frank_engineer: hotfix patch (applied):

```
--- a/serve/cache.go
+++ b/serve/cache.go
@@
- if enablePrefixCache {
-   val := prefixCache.Get(k)
- }
+ // temporary: bypass prefix cache until tokenizer rollback confirmed
+ enablePrefixCache = false
```

incident-bot: Hotfix applied, restart of serve pods initiated.

ben_sre: metrics: 5xx rate dropping to 1.2% after flags; p95 down to 6.1s. KV nodes mem stabilizing. Keep observing for next 10m.

eve_support: Customer note: CS triage: two enterprise customers reported degraded responses and one brief outage window (~6m). No data loss. Flagging for post-incident follow-up and possible SLA credit discussion.

alice_oncall: good catch. Start timeline and impact log. Who can take ownership for tokenizer regression and model-serving config? @carmen_ml?

carmen_ml: I'll lead root cause. Early hypothesis: tokenizer normalization change introduced a non-deterministic byte sequence for certain Unicode sequences in prompt templates -> hash variance. Need to correlate model version -> tokenizer commit -> serving config. I'll produce a PR to pin tokenizer version in serving and a canary test.

devon_platform: I'm going to rollback the tokenizer rollout in the canary cluster and pin upstream config to previous stable deploy. Will coordinate with carmen.

frank_engineer: creating a recovery checklist and will add a safeguard: metric alert for rapid growth in unique prompthash keys (rate > 2000/hr) and auto-disable continuous_batching if triggered.

alice_oncall: okay, summary for handoff to next oncall (ben_sre taking over at shift change in 20m):
- Incident: KV prefix cache blowup due to prompthash drift + continuous batching amplification
- Impact: p95 latency spike to 9.8s, 5xx peaked 3.4%, ~10% requests affected, 2 enterprise customers reported issues
- Mitigations applied: disabled continuous_batching in prod-us-west-2, reduced max_batch_size, forced prefix_cache TTL to 300s, hotfix to bypass local prefix cache, restart serve pods, rollback tokenizer canary
- Status: metrics improving (5xx -> 0.9% currently), KV mem usage trending down, hotfix in prod, root cause investigation in progress
- Open actions: tokenization root cause RCA (owner: carmen_ml), add auto-safeguard for unique-key surge (owner: frank_engineer), CS follow-up and SLA review (owner: eve_support), postmortem doc draft (owner: alice_oncall)

ben_sre: taking handoff. I'll keep monitoring the runbook checklist and verify the auto-scrub did not cause customer cache misses. any extra notes?

eve_support: I'll reach out to impacted customers with incident summary template, timeframe, and mitigation steps. Will coordinate with product for SLA impact.

carmen_ml: immediate next steps for me: gather tokenizer diffs, reproduce local prompthash variance with test corpus, add unit tests to prevent non-deterministic tokenization. ETA 48h for root cause and patch. Posting links to PRs in thread when ready.

frank_engineer: I'll write the alert and a runbook entry for this failure mode and propose a safer rollout pattern for tokenizer updates.

alice_oncall: thanks team. adding :white_check_mark: to timeline and will open postmortem. handing to ben for watch.

ben_sre: acknowledged. putting pager on watch and will escalate if 5xx > 1.5% sustained.

incident-bot: Incident downgraded to watch. Tags: kv-cache, batching, tokenizer, customer-impact. Handoff complete.

alice_oncall: final note: please add any logs/commands you ran to the postmortem doc. closing thread for now; reopen if regressions reappear. :thumbsup:
